dataset.datasetnotes:
This dataset is part of a group of Vermont (VT; USA) datasets contributed by Kellie Merrell of the Vermont Department of Environmental Conservation and colleagues to be used in the Northeast Lake Sediment Diatom Collaborative (NLSDC).

All counts were performed by Paul Garrison.  To help provide taxonomic consistency with other VT datasets, he changed the original taxa names he used, to the extent possible, to those determined in the Northeast Lake Voucher Flora project (NLVF), which was based on the analysis of diatoms from 100 EPA National Lake Assessment (NLA) 2017 study lakes in the northeast US.  The Voucher Flora is consistent with, and documented at, the Diatoms of North America website (https://instaar.colorado.edu/uploads/research/Northeast_Lakes_Voucher_Flora_Future_Edition.zip) as of April 2020.  Documentation includes many photographs.  Names for undescribed taxa, not included in the NEVF were made equivalent to names in the Neotoma master-list of diatom taxa.  A file was created showing corresponding names for taxa (Original with authorities, NLVF names and OTU codes, Neotoma master-list, and name entered into Neotoma).
This dataset was originally uploaded to the Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University constituent database, which was merged into the Diatom Paleolimnology Data Cooperative (DPDC) constituent database in July 2026.

Description of sampling from Davis et al 1994 CJFAS, p. 1856:  
"Most of the lakes were sampled three times in 1983 and four times in 1984, during the ice-free seasons, and in accord with protocols of the Paleoecological Investigation of Recent Lake Acidification (PIRLA) 
(Charles and Whitehead 1986;Norton et al. 1986). Fourteen of the lakes in New Hampshire and Vermont were sampled only in 1984. For some lakes,
occasional non-PIRLA data from 1978 to 1980 (Norton et al.1981) and from 1988 to 1984 (Buso et al. 1984; Haines et al. 1984; Kahl et al. 1985) were added. The non-PIRLA data were collected in accord with USEPA protocols and, like the PIRLA data, were subjected to rigorous quality control and assurance."

From Charles and Whitehead 1986, p. 16-19, N NE Water Chemistry methods:
"All sampling was conducted where the water depth was at least 90 percent of maximum.  A YSI O2 temperature meter and probe were used to establish the depth of stratified water (top of metalimnion), if present.  Only the mixed part of the water column was sampled, using a 9 mm I.D. flexible Tygon tube to a maximum depth of 2 m above the sediment.  
Water column samples were taken from a minimum of five different locations over the deepest part of the lake and combined in a four liter linear polyethelene (LPE) collection bottle.  At remote lakes less than three meters deep, samples were taken by hand dipping directly into sample bottles from approximately 0.5 m depth."

Sample collections were made by various combinations of the project investigators, helped by field assistants.

dataset.datasetname: Northeast Diatom Voucher Flora surface sample dataset
dataset.datasetnotes:
All lakes were sampled as part of the US EPA's 2017 National Lake Assessment.

Surface sediment samples were collected by crews from individual state agencies at the time they were doing other sampling for the EPA National Lake Survey.  Samples from sediment core intervals 0-1 and 1-2 cm were both saved.  Diatom analysis was performed on the combined material from both intervals (0-2 cm).  No core material was saved for future analysis.

No data on lake or watershed characteristics were available from EPA at the time data were entered into Neotoma (November 2018).  Data are expected to be available in the future at: https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/nla
-------

From NE Voucher flora website:https://diatoms.org/projects/northeast-lakes-regional-flora

"This project is a model for ensuring taxonomic consistency across analysts by 1) use of Battarbee Chambers, 2) randomizing sample assignment to analysts, 3) developing a pre-voucher flora, 4) coordinating analysts through weekly webinars, 5) ensuring 20% repeat counts (10% and self 10% cross QA/QC), 6) documenting taxon names and sources, and 7) thorough project documentation.

1) Sediments from 106 lakes in the northeast were processed to produce quantitative slides, through the use of Battarbee Chambers.

2) The samples, along with 6 replicate samples, were randomized for assignment to 3 analysts.

3) A pre-voucher flora based on over 4000 digital images was developed to represent the taxonomic diversity and morphologic range of species.

4) Seven weekly webinars were held for analysts to discuss problematic taxa and highlight new taxa added to the flora as they were encountered. Newly encountered taxa were imaged and incorporated into a weekly updated flora. We led a workshop with the analysts and other interested experts at the Diatom Herbarium at the Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia on March 27-30, 2018 to assign species names and resolve difficult species boundaries in this project. 

5) A rigorous QA/QC procedure documents analyst self consistency and cross analyst consistency.

6, 7) The flora, taxon names, references and R scripts documenting the project and preparing the data for analysis are available at the INSTAAR link. 

Funding
US Environmental Protection Agency
Regional Voucher Flora and taxon webpages for North Eastern Lakes - Sarah Spaulding
--------------
A set of slides is archived in the Diatom Herbarium at the Academy of Natural Sciences
This dataset was originally uploaded to the Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University constituent database, which was merged into the Diatom Paleolimnology Data Cooperative (DPDC) constituent database in July 2026.

All lakes were sampled as part of the US EPA's 2017 National Lake Assessment.

Surface sediment samples were collected by crews from individual state agencies at the time they were doing other sampling for the EPA National Lake Survey.  Samples from sediment core intervals 0-1 and 1-2 cm were both saved.  Diatom analysis was performed on the combined material from both intervals (0-2 cm).  No core material was saved for future analysis.

No data on lake or watershed characteristics were available from EPA at the time data were entered into Neotoma (November 2018).  Data are expected to be available in the future at: https://www.epa.gov/national-aquatic-resource-surveys/nla

From NE Voucher flora website:https://diatoms.org/projects/northeast-lakes-regional-flora

"This project is a model for ensuring taxonomic consistency across analysts by 1) use of Battarbee Chambers, 2) randomizing sample assignment to analysts, 3) developing a pre-voucher flora, 4) coordinating analysts through weekly webinars, 5) ensuring 20% repeat counts (10% and self 10% cross QA/QC), 6) documenting taxon names and sources, and 7) thorough project documentation.

1) Sediments from 106 lakes in the northeast were processed to produce quantitative slides, through the use of Battarbee Chambers.

2) The samples, along with 6 replicate samples, were randomized for assignment to 3 analysts.

3) A pre-voucher flora based on over 4000 digital images was developed to represent the taxonomic diversity and morphologic range of species.

4) Seven weekly webinars were held for analysts to discuss problematic taxa and highlight new taxa added to the flora as they were encountered. Newly encountered taxa were imaged and incorporated into a weekly updated flora. We led a workshop with the analysts and other interested experts at the Diatom Herbarium at the Academy of Natural Sciences in Philadelphia on March 27-30, 2018 to assign species names and resolve difficult species boundaries in this project. 

5) A rigorous QA/QC procedure documents analyst self consistency and cross analyst consistency.

6, 7) The flora, taxon names, references and R scripts documenting the project and preparing the data for analysis are available at the INSTAAR link. 

Funding
US Environmental Protection Agency
Regional Voucher Flora and taxon webpages for North Eastern Lakes - Sarah Spaulding

dataset.datasetnotes:
From Dixit et al 1999:
"In addition to various limnological measurements made in the field, water samples were collected for detailed chemical analysis (Baker et al. 1997). These water samples were taken from the 1.5-m water depth, or from the 0.5-m depth if the lake was <2 m deep. The details of field sampling protocols and methods used for the chemical analysis in EMAP-SW are presented in Baker et al. (1997). The EMAP-SW resource group provided all the necessary physical, chemical, and land use data for the study lakes. These data can be found on EMAP’s web site (http://www.epa.gov/emap/ html/dataI/surfwatr/data/nelakes)."

Each lake was sampled once at the same time the core was taken.
